title: Conversation Latency Matrix & Slicer with Streaming Toggle
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a composite dashboard (Conversation Latency Matrix) that allows engineers and PMs to slice latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) by model and route and to toggle streaming vs non-streaming I/O modes. The dashboard must combine tracing hooks, metrics pipelines, and logs-derived error counts so that a single view surfaces tail behavior, cohort regressions, and correlated error spikes. This ticket covers data-pipeline mapping, query templates, dashboard panels, annotation/trace linking, and rollout to the observability namespace.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard exposes p50/p95/p99 for any model + route combination with a streaming/non-streaming toggle
Percentiles are computed from histogram buckets emitted by runtime or derived from trace timing when histograms are missing
Each chart includes links to example traces (OpenTelemetry trace id) when a percentile spike is selected
Error-rate overlays and count panels show HTTP 5xx and runtime errors per cohort
Dashboard supports pre-configured cohorts: short-conv (<128 tokens), medium (128-512), long (>512), and open custom filter
Runbook entry created with recommended alert thresholds and SLO references
technical_notes: We will reuse the existing telemetry path: runtime emits prometheus histograms (redwood_request_latency_bucket) with labels {model, route, io_mode, request_shape}. Traces created by the serving runtime include span attributes span.kind=server, model.name, route.id, io_mode, tokens_requested, tokens_served. For streaming, the runtime will emit additional span events for first-byte and final-byte timestamps. If histogram data is sparse for low-volume routes, fallback to aggregating trace durations via trace processor and synthesize histogram buckets. Use Grafana Loki for logs correlation and Tempo for traces. Quantile calculations will prefer Prometheus histogram_quantile with pre-aggregated histogram buckets; fallback path will use TDigest in the trace-aggregation job. Instrumentation PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4121
decisions: Use Prometheus histograms as primary source for p50/p95/p99 to keep realtime computations cheap
Add an io_mode label (streaming|sync) to all latency metrics and traces - consistent with existing route tagging
When histograms are missing, run a 5m batch trace aggregation job to approximate percentiles instead of doing heavy per-query trace joins
blockers: Runtime needs a small telemetry change to emit io_mode for legacy routes (ENG-271999 created to track runtime work)
Tempo trace retention for low-volume customers is 7 days; need confirmation whether 30-day retention required for prolonged regression analysis
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy telemetry change to staging (runtime canary) 2) Run trace-aggregation job for staging to populate fallback histograms 3) Import dashboard in staging Grafana and validate panels with staging traffic 4) Run a 48h bake with alert thresholds in monitor-only 5) Roll to production with canary routes enabled
testing_plan: Synthetic traffic generator will produce streaming and sync requests across model families (small, medium, large). Validate percentiles against ground-truth measured by the generator. Add unit tests for histogram-to-quantile query templates and integration test that verifies trace linking for a selected p99 bucket.
notes_for_reviewers: Please review the histogram label strategy: we currently use request_shape (short/med/long) and plan to add tokens_requested label for finer slicing. Concern: cardinality growth if we add tokens_requested as a label; prefer using request_shape for dashboards and tokens_requested only in traces.
